faqItems.q: How is dinecue different from a map search?
faqItems.a: Map search answers “what is near me”. dinecue answers “what fits tonight”. It reads your mood, who you are with, your budget and the occasion together, then returns a short set of places with the reason each one works.

faqItems.q: Do I have to fill in a long form?
faqItems.a: No. You can describe the meal in one sentence. Location, party size and meal moment are optional refinements, not required fields.

faqItems.q: How many recommendations do I get?
faqItems.a: Up to three. dinecue narrows the field on purpose — a short list you can act on beats an endless one you scroll past.
Yes. You can type a location, drop a pin on the map, or use your current position, so dinecue works in a city you have never eaten in.
The free plan includes five dining decisions per month. A Pro plan with fifty decisions per month is coming; there is no checkout yet, so nothing to pay for today.
English, Turkish and German. You can switch language at any time, and a signed-in account remembers your choice.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms explain how you may use dinecue, a dining decision assistant that helps you compare restaurants and meal options by context.

sections.title: Acceptance of Terms
sections.body: By using dinecue, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

sections.title: What dinecue Does
sections.body: dinecue helps you decide where to eat by considering your mood, location, preferences, dining context and available place information.

sections.title: Accounts and Sign-in
sections.body: You can sign in with an email one-time code or Google Sign-In. dinecue does not offer password login in this version.

sections.title: Recommendations and Third-Party Data
sections.body: Recommendations may use third-party services and publicly available place information. dinecue may not know every detail about a restaurant, menu, price, reservation or availability.

sections.title: User Inputs and Preferences
sections.body: You are responsible for the information you enter, including location, preferences, dining context and menu or restaurant details.

sections.title: Fair Use and Quotas
sections.body: The Free plan includes limited monthly use. Pro may be offered later, but dinecue does not currently promise a paid upgrade or payment flow.

sections.title: No Guarantees
sections.body: dinecue does not guarantee that a recommendation will be perfect, available, open, affordable, safe for every diet, or suitable for every situation.

sections.title: Health, Diet and Allergy Notice
sections.body: dinecue is not medical advice. For allergies, dietary restrictions, pregnancy, medical conditions or religious requirements, confirm details directly with the restaurant or a qualified professional.

sections.title: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, dinecue is not liable for decisions, losses or issues arising from restaurant visits, third-party information or user-provided inputs.

sections.title: Changes to the Service
sections.body: dinecue may change features, limits, availability and these terms as the product evolves.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Questions about these terms can be sent to hello@dinecue.com.

privacy.seoDescription: Learn how dinecue handles account, preference, location, restaurant context, cookie, and third-party service information.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains the information dinecue may collect and how it is used to provide a more useful dining decision experience.

sections.title: Information We Collect
sections.body: dinecue may collect account details such as email, display name, preferred language, country, currency and distance unit, along with inputs you provide while using the product.

sections.title: How We Use Information
sections.body: We use information to sign you in, personalize recommendations, remember preferences, manage quotas, improve reliability and keep the service secure.

sections.title: Authentication
sections.body: Email sign-in uses one-time codes. Google Sign-In may provide your email and basic profile details so dinecue can create or restore your account.

sections.title: Restaurant, Location and Preference Data
sections.body: You may enter location, restaurant, menu, taste and dining preference information. This is used to make recommendations more relevant.

sections.title: Cookies and Local Storage
sections.body: dinecue uses secure cookies for sign-in and local storage for harmless interface preferences such as language before sign-in.

sections.title: Third-Party Services
sections.body: Recommendations may involve third-party services for place information and language-based reasoning. Provider keys are not exposed in the browser.

sections.title: Data Retention
sections.body: dinecue keeps account and recommendation information only as needed to operate the product, support history and saved places, and maintain safety and reliability.

sections.title: User Choices
sections.body: You can update profile preferences, sign out, and choose what information you enter. More account controls may be added as the product matures.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: dinecue is designed so sensitive sign-in tokens are kept in httpOnly cookies and are not available to browser JavaScript.

sections.title: Children’s Privacy
sections.body: dinecue is not designed for children. If you believe a child has provided personal information, contact us.

sections.title: Changes to This Policy
sections.body: We may update this policy as dinecue changes. The latest version will be posted here.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Privacy questions can be sent to hello@dinecue.com.

about.seoDescription: Learn what dinecue is, why it exists, and how it helps travelers and local diners make better restaurant decisions.
about.title: Not just where to eat, but why it fits you.
about.intro: dinecue is a dining decision assistant for people who want fewer tabs, fewer guesses and a calmer way to choose a restaurant.

sections.title: What is dinecue?
sections.body: dinecue helps you choose restaurants and meal options by combining what you want right now with practical context such as location, company, budget, preferences and appetite.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: Choosing where to eat is rarely just a search problem. dinecue exists for the moment when ratings, photos and endless lists are not enough to answer whether a place fits tonight.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: You describe the meal you want. dinecue shapes that context into a small set of places or choices, explains why they fit, and stays honest when something is uncertain.

sections.title: Built for travelers and everyday dining decisions
sections.body: dinecue is useful when you are traveling, planning dinner, comparing local places, checking whether a restaurant fits your mood, or trying to make a menu easier to understand.

sections.title: Contact / Creator
sections.body: dinecue is created as a focused dining product with a warm, practical point of view. For contact or creator information, visit burak-altintas.com.
